verdict.rationale: Ironclad shows some template-creation capability (No-Code Builder, template IDs, and historical NDA/contract templates referenced in HN threads), suggesting founders could generate routine documents without starting from scratch. However, the bulk of the evidence positions Ironclad as an enterprise CLM/workflow platform rather than a curated 'vetted library' for pre-counsel document creation, and community comments raise unresolved questions about whether the 'industry standard' templates are legally vetted (e.g. malpractice-insurance question, Delaware C-Corp limitation) that are never answered in the pack. Missing for 10: clear evidence of a curated/vetted template library (breadth of NDAs, policies, agreements) explicitly marketed for non-lawyer founders, and confirmation that templates are legally reviewed/vetted rather than generic no-code contract building blocks.
